In [[differential geometry]], the '''Kosmann lift''',<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fatibene |first1=L. |last2=Ferraris |first2=M. |last3=Francaviglia |first3=M. |last4=Godina |first4=M. |year=1996 |chapter=A geometric definition of Lie derivative for Spinor Fields |title=Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Differential Geometry and Applications, August 28th–September 1st 1995 (Brno, Czech Republic) |editor-last=Janyska |editor-first=J. |editor2-last=Kolář |editor2-first=I. |editor3-last=Slovák |editor3-first=J. |publisher=Masaryk University |location=Brno |pages=549–558 |isbn=80-210-1369-9 |arxiv=gr-qc/9608003v1 |bibcode=1996gr.qc.....8003F }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Godina |first1=M. |last2=Matteucci |first2=P. |year=2003 |title=Reductive G-structures and Lie derivatives |journal=[[Journal of Geometry and Physics]] |volume=47 |issue=1 |pages=66–86 |doi=10.1016/S0393-0440(02)00174-2 |arxiv=math/0201235 |bibcode=2003JGP....47...66G }}</ref> named after [[Yvette Kosmann-Schwarzbach]], of a vector field <math>X\,</math> on a [[Riemannian manifold]] <math>(M,g)\,</math> is the canonical projection <math>X_{K}\,</math> on the [[orthonormal frame bundle]] of its natural lift <math>\hat{X}\,</math> defined on the bundle of linear frames.<ref>{{citation | last1=Kobayashi|first1=Shoshichi|last2=Nomizu|first2=Katsumi | title = Foundations of Differential Geometry|volume=1| publisher=Wiley-Interscience | year=1996|isbn=0-470-49647-9}} (''Example'' 5.2) pp. 55-56</ref>

Generalisations exist for any given reductive [[G-structure]].

==Introduction==
In general, given a [[subbundle]] <math>Q\subset E\,</math> of a [[fiber bundle]] <math>\pi_{E}\colon E\to M\,</math> over <math>M</math> and a vector field <math>Z\,</math> on <math>E</math>, its restriction <math>Z\vert_Q\,</math> to <math>Q</math> is a vector field "along" <math>Q</math> not ''on'' (i.e., ''tangent'' to) <math>Q</math>. If one denotes by <math>i_{Q} \colon Q\hookrightarrow  E</math> the canonical [[embedding]], then <math>Z\vert_Q\,</math> is a [[Section (fiber bundle)|section]] of the [[pullback bundle]] <math>i^{\ast}_{Q}(TE) \to Q\,</math>, where
:<math>i^{\ast}_{Q}(TE) = \{(q,v) \in Q \times TE \mid i(q) = \tau_{E}(v)\}\subset Q\times TE,\,</math>
and <math>\tau_{E}\colon TE\to E\,</math> is the [[tangent bundle]] of the fiber bundle <math>E</math>.
Let us assume that we are given a ''' Kosmann decomposition''' of the pullback bundle <math>i^{\ast}_{Q}(TE) \to Q\,</math>,  such that
:<math>i^{\ast}_{Q}(TE) = TQ\oplus \mathcal M(Q),\,</math>
i.e., at each <math>q\in Q</math> one has <math>T_qE=T_qQ\oplus \mathcal M_u\,,</math> where <math>\mathcal M_{u}</math> is a [[vector subspace]] of  <math>T_qE\,</math> and we assume <math>\mathcal M(Q)\to Q\,</math> to be a [[vector bundle]] over <math>Q</math>, called the '''transversal bundle''' of the ''' Kosmann decomposition'''. It follows that the restriction <math>Z\vert_Q\,</math> to <math>Q</math> splits into a ''tangent'' vector field <math>Z_K\,</math> on <math>Q</math> and a ''transverse'' vector field <math>Z_G,\,</math> being a section of the vector bundle <math>\mathcal M(Q)\to Q.\,</math>

==Definition==

Let <math>\mathrm F_{SO}(M)\to M</math> be the oriented [[orthonormal frame bundle]] of an oriented <math>n</math>-dimensional 
Riemannian manifold <math>M</math> with given metric <math>g\,</math>. This is a principal <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)\,</math>-subbundle of <math>\mathrm FM\,</math>, the [[tangent frame bundle]] of linear frames over <math>M</math> with structure group <math>{\mathrm G\mathrm L}(n,\mathbb R)\,</math>.
By definition, one may say that we are given with a classical reductive <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)\,</math>-structure. The special orthogonal group <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)\,</math> is a reductive Lie subgroup of <math>{\mathrm G\mathrm L}(n,\mathbb R)\,</math>. In fact, there exists a [[direct sum]] decomposition <math>\mathfrak{gl}(n)=\mathfrak{so}(n)\oplus \mathfrak{m}\,</math>, where <math>\mathfrak{gl}(n)\,</math> is the [[Lie algebra]] of <math>{\mathrm G\mathrm L}(n,\mathbb R)\,</math>, <math>\mathfrak{so}(n)\,</math> is the Lie algebra of <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)\,</math>, and <math>\mathfrak{m}\,</math> is the <math>\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathrm S\mathrm O}\,</math>-invariant vector subspace of [[Symmetric matrix|symmetric matrices]], i.e. <math>\mathrm{Ad}_{a}\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}\,</math> for all <math>a\in{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)\,.</math>

Let <math>i_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)} \colon \mathrm F_{SO}(M)\hookrightarrow  \mathrm FM</math> be the canonical [[embedding]].
 
One then can prove that there exists a canonical '''Kosmann decomposition''' of the [[pullback bundle]] <math>i^{\ast}_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)}(T\mathrm FM) \to \mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math> such that

:<math>i^{\ast}_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)}(T\mathrm FM)=T\mathrm F_{SO}(M)\oplus \mathcal M(\mathrm F_{SO}(M))\,,</math>

i.e., at each <math>u\in \mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math> one has <math>T_u\mathrm FM=T_u \mathrm F_{SO}(M)\oplus \mathcal M_u\,,</math> <math>\mathcal M_{u}</math> being the fiber over <math>u</math> of the [[subbundle]] <math>\mathcal M(\mathrm F_{SO}(M))\to \mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math> of <math>i^{\ast}_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)}(V\mathrm FM) \to \mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math>. Here, <math>V\mathrm FM\,</math> is the vertical subbundle of <math>T\mathrm FM\,</math> and at each <math>u\in \mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math> the fiber <math>\mathcal M_{u}</math> is isomorphic to the [[vector space]] of symmetric matrices <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>.

From the above canonical and [[equivariant]] decomposition, it follows that the restriction <math>Z\vert_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)}</math> of an <math>{\mathrm G\mathrm L}(n,\mathbb R)</math>-invariant vector field <math>Z\,</math> on <math>\mathrm FM</math> to <math>\mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math> splits into a <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)</math>-invariant vector field <math>Z_{K}\,</math> on <math>\mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math>, called the '''Kosmann vector field associated with''' <math>Z\,</math>, and a ''transverse'' vector field <math>Z_{G}\,</math>.

In particular, for a generic [[vector field]] <math>X\,</math> on the base manifold <math>(M,g)\,</math>, it follows that the restriction <math>\hat{X}\vert_{\mathrm F_{SO}(M)}\,</math> to <math>\mathrm F_{SO}(M)\to M</math> of its natural lift <math>\hat{X}\,</math> onto <math>\mathrm FM\to M</math> splits into a <math>{\mathrm S\mathrm O}(n)</math>-invariant vector field <math>X_{K}\,</math> on <math>\mathrm F_{SO}(M)</math>, called the '''Kosmann lift''' of <math>X\,</math>, and a ''transverse'' vector field <math>X_{G}\,</math>.
